title: The Kites: the last two stanzas
body:
In the poem 'The Kites' by Daphne Lister, a child watches kites flying in a windy sky and wishes to be small and light enough to climb on one. The last two stanzas imagine the ride:

What fun it would be
To look right down,
Over the park
And the rooftops of town.

The people below
Would stand and stare,
And wish they were me
High, high in the air.
